artboards.title: Proposed — a band filtered, and a balance that disagrees
Proposed — the one change to Chase debts
Proposed — settled, not started, and failed to load

annotations.text:
THE JOB OF THIS SCREEN

You settled three things, and everything here follows from them:

1. TWO SCREENS, ONE SEQUENCE. Debtors is the whole book — the position, the age of the money, search, the band filter, print, and the place a payment is received. Chase debts stays the queue and the words, and gains one read-only reading of the age split that links back here. There is exactly one age filter in the app, and it lives on the screen that owns the whole book.

2. THE ACCENT IS "RECEIVE A PAYMENT". Money coming in is the outcome this screen produces, so oxide appears once, on that button, inside the one open row. Print, Export, statement and the drift repairs are all plain.

3. PRINT WHAT IS ON SCREEN. Whatever the search and the band have left, with the filter named on the sheet so a printed page says what it is.

AND THE TITLE IS NOW "DEBTORS" — which fixes a real inconsistency, not just a preference. The rail says "Who owes you", the heading says "Debtors list", the breadcrumb says "Who owes you". Three names for one screen. The old names stay as search keywords, so typing either word still finds it.

Everything is drawn from index.html's own values: the 23-colour palette, the 11/12/13/14 ramp, Inter + Archivo Black + IBM Plex Mono, and the .ow-* console components already shipping on Today, Chase debts, Follow-ups and Consignment. No new colour, no new weight, no new type size, no fourteenth button family.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT AS IT STANDS →

1. THREE NAMES FOR ONE SCREEN. Rail: "Who owes you". Heading: "Debtors list". Breadcrumb: "Who owes you". Whichever you standardise on, this is a defect.

2. THE HEADLINE FIGURE IS IN THE WRONG FACE. .age-pos-total b sets 8,420,000 in Archivo Black at 34px. Archivo Black is loaded for PAGE NAMES ONLY; money is IBM Plex Mono, tabular. So the single most important figure on the screen is in the one face the system forbids for figures — and it asks for tabular-nums from a face that has no real tabular set. 34px is not on the ramp either.

3. THE SAME FACT, TWICE, ON EVERY ROW. The age band is carried by a coloured pill AND a 3px coloured stripe on the first cell. Two devices, one fact — and because every row has an age, every row is coloured. A device that marks everything marks nothing.

4. THE BAR AND THE BAND CARDS ARE ALSO THE SAME THING TWICE. A 16px stacked bar, then five bordered cards with 3px top-caps repeating the same five figures, and both are the filter. That is ~120px of vertical space spent saying one thing in two voices.

5. FIVE STATE COLOURS, ONE OF THEM THE ACCENT. .age-b90 paints 60–90 days in oxide-light. The palette has three state colours — verdigris, amber, crimson — and oxide is the accent, not a state. So the accent fires as a band colour, on a stripe, and on .age-name:hover.

6. THE ACCENT IS SPENT ON NOTHING. btn-accent appears nowhere on this screen. "Receive" — the one act that puts money in the drawer — is a 12px grey text link in the last table cell, quieter than "Export CSV".

7. THE CONTROLS DO NOT LOOK LIKE CONTROLS. Search sits in a .field with a floating 12px label inside an .an-toolbar — form furniture, not a list toolbar. "Hide no debt" is a bare checkbox nudged with padding-bottom:9px. Export and Print are up in the panel head, 24px and one heading away from the list they act on, above the search box that decides what they will contain. You asked me to add filter, print and search: all four already exist. This is why you could not find them.

8. EVERYTHING IS WEIGHT 700. .age-name, .age-amt, .age-band-amt, .age-band-label, .age-pill, .age-never, th, and the total row. When everything is bold, nothing is.

9. OFF-SYSTEM VALUES THROUGHOUT. Sizes 10.5, 11.5, 12.5, 13.5, 16, 17, 34 — of which one is on the ramp. Radii 10, 12 and 999 where the system is 4/6/8. A drop shadow on .panel where depth in this app is hairlines. 22/24px panel padding, so the two panels spend 88px of height on air before any content.

10. A 150-CHARACTER PARAGRAPH IN THE PAGE HEAD, unmeasured, at 14px. The console header is a name, one line, a hairline; the long version goes behind the "i".

11. SIX COLUMNS AND NO ROOM. "Paid off" reserves 112px on every row for a percentage of a balance — a per-customer read, not a scanning column — and it pushed the customer name into wrapping. Money never truncates; names do.

THE PROPOSAL — what changed, and why

THE STRIP ANSWERS FOUR QUESTIONS AND NOT ONE MORE. What you are owed (ink — being owed money is a fact, not a warning); how much of it is over 90 days (crimson, with its share, because that is the genuinely bad news and it was previously a paragraph); the largest single debt (how exposed you are to one name); and how much has no date behind it (amber — a figure whose age cannot be derived, and this is the only screen that can repair it). Tile 1 says out loud that it is the whole book whatever the list is filtered to, which is the promise the old code made in a comment and never on screen.

ONE DEVICE FOR THE AGE, NOT TWO. The bar keeps the proportion — flex-grow on shillings, so one big old balance looks like the problem it is — and the five bordered cards become a legend under it: a 2px cap, the band, the figure, the count. Same information, same click targets, roughly half the height, and the legend is plainly subordinate to the bar instead of competing with it. Clicking either filters the list; clicking again clears it, so the way out is the way in.

THE BANDS ARE NOW THREE COLOURS, NOT FIVE. Grey under 30 days, amber 30–60, crimson 60 and over, pale grey for no-date. Oxide is not a band any more. Nothing is coloured for merely existing.

A ROW SAYS THE AGE ONCE. 44px, opens in place: name and place, how far through the balance they are, when they last paid anything, then the figure right-aligned in tabular mono with its BASIS underneath — "owing 94 days" — and that basis line is the only place age lives. It is crimson past 60 days, amber past 30 and inside "age not on record", ink otherwise. So the column reads as a ranking and the colour in it means something.

"LAST PAID" EARNS ITS COLUMN. It is the best single read on whether somebody has gone quiet, and "Never paid" is crimson because it is the one value in that column worth stopping on — a customer who never started is a different thing from one who has gone quiet, and only the first is a reason not to sell to them again.

THE TOOLBAR IS A TOOLBAR. Search with a magnifier in it, a real toggle, then Print and Export pushed right — all in one 46px band directly above the rows they act on. Print says "Print these 3" when a band is on (see page 2), because a printed sheet should never be ambiguous about what it contains.

THE ACCENT APPEARS ONCE: "Receive a payment", inside the one open row, beside the invoices it will clear. The open row is where the screen earns its keep — the three invoices behind the balance, with charged, paid and still-open on each, so you can see WHY the figure is 1,640,000 before you ask anyone for it.

THE RAIL CARRIES THE REASONING, MEASURED. How a balance is worked out (charges not yet paid, walked oldest first — which is why the age is the age of the money and not of their last visit); three derived figures; and the handoff: Chase debts has the 6 past your terms with the words already written. That is the sequence, stated, instead of two screens that look like each other.

HEIGHT: the position went from ~430px to ~230px, so eight debtors are on the first screen instead of two.

A BAND FILTERED, AND A BALANCE THAT DISAGREES →

THE FILTER IS VISIBLE IN THREE PLACES AT ONCE, and that is deliberate: the segment and its legend entry are ringed, an amber chip sits in the toolbar with its own ✕, and a hairline note where the missing rows would have been says exactly what is hidden — "11 customers owing 6,240,000". A filter you cannot see is a filter you forget you set, and then you trust a total that is a slice.

THE STRIP DOES NOT MOVE. Still 8,420,000 across 14 customers. Your own code says why: "a position that shrinks because somebody left a filter on is a position nobody can trust."

PRINT SAYS "PRINT THESE 3". You chose print-what-is-on-screen, so the button counts what it will print and the sheet carries the filter at the top. A printed page with no idea what it contains is worse than no printed page.

THE DRIFT BAND IS AMBER, NOT OXIDE. A balance that does not match its own history is a caution with a fix attached, not the screen's one action. It names the customer, both figures and the gap; it says what it means (a payment taken without being written down); and it says the consequence that matters — Chase debts will not write a demand for a figure the shop cannot explain. Both repairs are ghost buttons because each is a decision about one named person, and the two verdicts routinely disagree.

That row's progress cell reads "nothing to measure" rather than a bar at 0%. A bar at zero would be a claim about somebody's conduct the records do not support.

THE ONE CHANGE TO CHASE DEBTS →

You asked whether the age bar could move here and let the two screens become one. I recommended against merging, and you agreed — this is the version of your idea that does not break either screen.

WHAT IS ADDED: one panel, between the strip and the queue, carrying the age of EVERYTHING you are owed. Same bar, same legend, same figures as Debtors — read from the same debAgingProfile(), so the two screens cannot disagree by construction.

WHAT IT IS NOT: a filter. This queue is built from your terms, the rest period and who has named a day. If an age band could narrow it, the queue would stop being the day's work and the strip above it would start describing a slice of the shop rather than the shop. So the bar reads, and clicking a band OPENS DEBTORS filtered to it — one filter, on the screen that owns the whole book, reachable from both.

WHY IT IS LABELLED "THE WHOLE BOOK — NOT JUST THIS QUEUE": because the queue is 6 customers and 5,210,000, and the bar totals 14 and 8,420,000. Without that line somebody would read the bar as this queue's age split, notice the figures do not add up to the strip, and stop trusting both. A figure on this app has to say what it is measuring.

Everything else on the screen is untouched: the strip, the queue, "Deliberately not asked", and the message composer stay exactly as they ship. The only other edit is one sentence in the held-back group, which currently says "fix it on Who owes you" and will say "fix it on Debtors".

THE THREE STATES A SCREEN IS ONLY DESIGNED ONCE YOU HAVE DRAWN →

NO STRIP OF ZEROS. Four tiles reading 0 is data slop: it fills a settled screen with figures that mean nothing and makes it look broken. One sentence, and "none" in the panel head, is the whole state.

SETTLED UP AND NOT STARTED ARE WORDED DIFFERENTLY, which the current code already gets right and is worth keeping: a shop on its first day has not settled up, it has not begun, and saying the first sentence to somebody with an empty book reads as the app misunderstanding what it is looking at. The second names the next action rather than describing itself.

THE THIRD STATE IS THE ONE THAT IS MISSING TODAY. If the customer ledger fails to read, this screen currently shows "Nobody owes you anything" — a failed load and a settled book are indistinguishable, and only one of them means you are owed nothing. That is the exact thing the app's own law forbids: a failure must name itself. So it says what failed, how long ago it last read, that these figures are not a position, and it turns Receive off rather than letting it fail halfway.

The rail still carries real figures on a settled book — what you collected and what you sold on credit this month — because "everything sold on credit this month has come back in" is the one reading of an empty debtors book that is worth anything.

All three are drawn stacked here so you can compare the wording. In the app only one is ever on screen.

THE PHONE — its own design, not the table reflowed

820px is a switch, so this is drawn from scratch at 390: 44px navy bar, 26px page name, 15px body, 14–16px row padding.

THE PHONE JOB IS LOOKING ONE CUSTOMER UP. Somebody is standing in the yard and you need their figure. So the search field is the first control under the strip, at 44px, before the list — the opposite of the desktop, where search sits above rows you are working down.

THE STRIP IS 2×2 IN ONE CARD with hairline dividers and no per-tile borders, carrying the same four figures.

THE BAR SURVIVES, THE LEGEND TURNS. Five bands across 358px is 60px each and unreadable, so the legend becomes two columns of band-and-figure. The bar itself is unchanged.

THE CARDS CARRY NO BUTTON. A card with a Receive button is ten oxide buttons on a screen allowed one, so the accent lives once, in the docked navy bar in the thumb zone — the pattern Follow-ups already ships. It names who the oldest money is with, so the default action is the right one without reading the list. Search for somebody and the dock follows the result.

NO FAKE CHROME: no painted status bar, no fake keyboard. On a real phone those render on top of the layout.

One thing to decide: whether the phone should let you RECEIVE a payment at all, or only read. Receiving posts to the cash book, and a mis-tap in a yard is a wrong ledger entry. I have drawn it enabled because collecting in the yard is exactly when money arrives — but say the word and it becomes read-only with the dock pointing at the desk.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DECIDED FOR YOU

1. THE OLD NAME. "Who owes you" and "Debtors list" stay as search keywords so the word already in somebody's head still finds the screen. Say if you want them dropped.

2. "HIDE SETTLED" replaces "Hide no debt", which read as a double negative. Same behaviour, on by default.

3. "PAID OFF" AS A COLUMN. You liked the progress bar, so it stays on the row — but as a track with a per-cent and no heading weight, and the figures it is measured from (420,000 of 2,060,000) moved into the open row where there is space to say what they are. If you would rather it left the row entirely, that is one line to remove.

4. THE THIRD RAIL PANEL ("What a payment does") is prose the current screen does not have. I added it because "a part payment keeps its original age rather than starting again" is a rule nothing on screen states, and it changes how somebody reads the age column. Cut it if the rail feels long.

5. WHAT I DID NOT TOUCH: the Creditors list — "Who you owe" — is this screen's twin and shares .age-* wholesale. Every fault above applies to it, and once this is built the same treatment is mostly mechanical. I have deliberately not drawn it: one screen at a time, and you may want to see this one working first.
